beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps the super-resolution image dense while a compact thought process updates it through shared recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method starts with a dense carrier because super-resolution needs spatial detail at every location. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing organizes those features without dropping the dense field. The DQ-CTM thought process reads and updates the carrier through repeated ticks. The decoder turns the updated dense representation back into the output image. The same DQ-CTM parameters are reused across ticks, so recurrence returns to the thought stage itself.

params.headline: ThinkSR routes dense features through shared thought ticks.
params.note: The loop returns to the DQ-CTM stage, not the full pipeline.

beats.intent: The carrier equation creates a dense feature field first, then partitions that field into windows while preserving tokens.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The equation makes the dense carrier explicit before the compact thought process touches it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window partition is applied to that field, keeping every token available to the model.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded before it is windowed.

terms.label: window partition keeps the dense tokens

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; at 1.129 million parameters, it is second largest among the five listed methods.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison keeps the benchmark honest by ordering the five reported models from smallest to largest. CATANet is the smallest at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN is close at 0.550 million. IMDN sits at 0.715 million. DQ-CTM-SR uses 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is largest at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is second largest in this five-method comparison.
params.note: Sorted by parameter count, smallest first.
